gen-dafont-dited-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads bookish and graceful, its strokes shifting weight without ever lurching. Dited is the one for digital, hip-to-hip display shapes with round letters opening wide, while Gambetta does its best work in tapering strokes, so the pair isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Cast-iron capitals, but in lowercase, drawn with compass-pencil consistency. Noto Sans Old Turkic follows with chunky, tall letters and curves that stay open, which is what makes the pairing approachable.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-gf-noto-sans: Towering lowercase, striding along with room to spare. Eight Bit Dragon does adventurous best, with gently modulated strokes and no sharp hairlines, while Noto Sans Tirhuta stays contemporary, its terminals cut back to leave big gaps around a dominant x-height.
